title: Israel’s Next Chapter: Election Results and the Road Ahead
gist: Israel's Oct. 27, 2026 election left both Netanyahu's bloc and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition alliance short of a parliamentary majority, setting up uncertain coalition talks. Al-Monitor hosted a panel on what the results mean for Israeli security policy, the Palestinians and ties with Washington.

insights.claim: In Israel's Oct. 27, 2026 election, neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot won a parliamentary majority.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Political deadlock prolongs policy uncertainty for Israeli assets and regional war/ceasefire decisions.

insights.claim: The election was the first national vote since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attacks and the ensuing regional war, making it a test of how three years of conflict reshaped Israeli politics.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Results gauge public appetite for continued war versus de-escalation.
